title: Best Laid Plans

beats.what: Jade and Boyd attempt to open the tunnel door in the basement; it is sealed, they leave a talisman on it
Boyd tells Henry and Victor about Tabitha's reincarnation memories; Henry erupts and refuses to hear it
Tabitha discloses to Julie and Ethan that she was Miranda; Julie challenges the claim, Ethan goes quiet
Victor arrives at Tabitha's house; insists on going to the car graveyard to find the yellow-suit man's vehicle
Boyd plans a night test of the totems against the creatures; describes running directly at one
Victor discovers a bag of teeth in the yellow-suit car; announces Ethan must be prepared because the pattern is repeating

character_beats.beat: Now in full operational mode after the trip's revelations; wants everyone aligned and moving fast, but Boyd keeps slowing the pace for safety checks that feel like stalling
Wants to warn Ethan about the man in yellow repeating the same massacre pattern, but telling Henry first destroyed that relay; he goes directly to the source
Wants to protect Miranda's memory and Victor's peace; his refusal of Tabitha's claim is grief, not logic, and he knows it

key_lines.line: You cannot save dead things. No matter how fucking smart you think you are.
key_lines.why: Henry's counter-thesis to the season's entire project; it also echoes the show's own existential doubt about whether the arc is solvable

key_lines.line: Every time someone here feels like they have a purpose, somebody always ends up dead.
key_lines.why: Julie names the pattern that makes every hopeful turn feel like a death sentence

key_lines.line: You came to town last time with a boy and a girl, and the man in yellow showed up. Everyone died.
key_lines.why: Victor completes the structural parallel that makes Ethan and Julie's presence a direct threat to themselves

open_loops: The bag of teeth in the yellow-suit car: whose teeth, and what do they signify about the man's nature?
Boyd plans a live test of the totems against the creatures tonight; the episode ends before the outcome
Henry has been approached by the man in yellow at the end of the episode
Donna remains unconscious at Colony House with no confirmed prognosis
Julie's mental state is fragile and she has not accepted Tabitha's disclosure

contradiction.wants: To protect Ethan from the pattern he knows is repeating by telling him what is coming
contradiction.does: Delivers the warning in a way that traumatizes rather than prepares, because his grief over Miranda's death overrides his capacity to calibrate the truth for a child

tone_notes: The 116-second silence from 07:03 to 09:00 dominates the episode's structure, landing immediately after Boyd and Jade abandon the sealed basement door. It is the longest silence of the final three episodes and sits in a double-zero density corridor (minutes 7 and 8 both read 0 words/min), suggesting the scene plays entirely on image and ambient sound. The back half of the episode is markedly denser, with minutes 15-17 peaking at 192-201 words/min during the family disclosure scene. Episode ends on a low-density stretch (minutes 47-50 range 14-68 words/min) as Henry encounters the man in yellow, letting dread accumulate slowly.
